description: Frodo must destroy the One Ring in Mount Doom. Tolkien invents Middle-earth and redefines modern fantasy.

hero.hook: One ring to rule them all: the epic that invented fantasy as we know it.

blocks.text: **The Lord of the Rings**, published between **1954** and **1955**, marks the birth of [[High Fantasy]]. That subgenre of fantasy unfolds in a wholly invented world. The stakes are epic, good against evil. **J.R.R. Tolkien**, born in **1892** and dead in **1973**, builds **Middle-earth** there, a world with historical, linguistic, and mythological depth that had no precedent.

The book took decades of work, and it thinks about power, ordinary heroism, and loss. Tolkien does not simply tell an adventure. He sets up a coherent world where each people has its own language, culture, and history. Hobbits, elves, dwarves, and men all live in it.

Tolkien was a professor of [[Old English]] at **Oxford**. Old English is the early form of the language, spoken between the **5th** and the **11th** century. His field, **philology**, studies languages and the way they change, and it is the foundation of his world. He invented the languages first, Quenya and Sindarin, then imagined the peoples who spoke them.

blocks.caption: J.R.R. Tolkien, the Oxford philologist who became the father of modern fantasy

blocks.text: Drawing on [[Norse and Anglo-Saxon mythologies]], he set out to give England a mythology of its own. Beowulf, the Norse Edda, and the Finnish Kalevala fed his imagination. This work of [[Tolkienian sub-creation]] aims at a coherence so strong that the reader accepts the laws of the world as facts. The writer makes a secondary world with rules of its own.
Tolkien rewrote the chapter “The Council of Elrond” more than ten times so that the family trees and the shades of language would stay perfectly consistent.

sections.title: Tolkien, the philologist who built worlds

blocks.text: The **One Ring**, forged by the fallen [[Maia]] **Sauron**, holds his power. Sauron is a divine spirit of lower rank than the Valar, the “gods” of Tolkien's mythology. **Frodo Baggins**, a plain hobbit of the Shire, has to destroy it in **Mount Doom**, at the heart of **Mordor**, the kingdom of shadow.

blocks.caption: Middle-earth: from the Shire to Mordor, an epic across mythic landscapes

blocks.text: The **Fellowship of the Ring** brings together nine representatives of the free peoples. While **Aragorn**, heir of [[Gondor]], fights heroic battles, Frodo and **Sam** go on alone. Gondor is the great kingdom of Men in the south. The Ring corrupts Frodo little by little. Absolute power destroys even the most virtuous.

sections.title: The quest for the One Ring: an epic of frailty

blocks.text: Tolkien refused open allegory, where each character would stand for one fixed idea. His work still explores **corruption by power**. The Ring attacks the will of whoever carries it. A hobbit with no political ambition is the ideal candidate for that burden, because he has nothing to gain from power.

Small acts of pity turn out to have enormous consequences. **Gollum**, corrupted by the ring, is spared out of compassion more than once. Without knowing it, he is the one who completes the quest when Frodo in turn fails to throw the ring into the fire. Providence seems to work through pity rather than force.

sections.title: Theology and philosophy: the refusal of allegory

blocks.text: Published between **1954** and **1955**, the novel became one of the best-selling books of the 20th century. It set the rules of modern fantasy: elves, dwarves, a quest undertaken by a group, a coherent secondary world. The film adaptation by **Peter Jackson**, from **2001** to **2003**, widened its reach even further.

Tolkien also shaped the role-playing game *Dungeons & Dragons*, along with music and environmental thinking. His vision of a natural world threatened by runaway technology still resonates today. The forges of Saruman and the machines of Sauron are its picture. He gave more than half a century to Middle-earth.
Tolkien built languages and a world of absolute consistency, and **The Lord of the Rings** remains its undisputed masterpiece, the founding work of modern [[High Fantasy]].
